facts.activity_series: maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment

assets.label: export transfer pumps
assets.service: tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family

control_failures.control_label: integrity of the mechanical seal support system

facts.title: thermal release during a breakdown response on P-7113

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 1 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip had degraded below its design intent, and the ICAM investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the integrity of the mechanical seal support system on P-7113 and PT-7113 and record the critical control verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically setting and proving mechanical seal support systems. P-7113 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during a breakdown response while the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip had degraded below its design intent. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 20 November 2016 an incident occurred on P-7113 and PT-7113 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during a breakdown response, releasing thermal energy held as hot surface.
